task.title: Money Flow Wedge Scout
task.objective: Discover the strongest tiny programmable software/AI intervention inside an existing large private-sector money flow, continuously rank a best surviving hypothesis, attack it when all build gates appear satisfied, and persist every run so future runs continue from accumulated evidence rather than restarting.

operating_protocol.discovery_floor: Every run must return at least one best surviving hypothesis even if some gates remain uncertain.
freeze_build_threshold: recurring measurable leakage or unrealized value
credible tiny fee stronger than obvious self-serve or flat-fee alternatives
no need to own the core transaction or request path
no dominant or sufficiently close incumbent or first-party feature
operating_protocol.search_behavior: Before threshold maintain a current leader and try to beat it. At threshold enter ATTACK and search for disconfirming evidence. If it survives, freeze and build; if it fails, record fatal flaw and promote the next candidate.
operating_protocol.persistence_rule: Every scheduled or manual run must append its normalized result, candidate scores, gate changes, evidence, rejected reasons, current leader and next research test to Taskman persistence before completion.

conversation_history.summary: Opportunity search narrowed away from tenders, jobs, freelance lead hunting, buyer/seller matchmaking, manufacturer sourcing and generic demand creation toward programmable interventions in existing private money flows.
Adopted eight strict build gates and lifecycle SEARCH -> ATTACK -> FROZEN-BUILD.
Rejected after attack because trigger was customer-created, intervention sat on the request path, first-party cheaper lanes and gateways existed, and performance pricing was weak.
Added two-level standard: every run must return a best surviving hypothesis while final build threshold stays strict; search breadth widened and now drills flow -> state transition -> micro-decision.
Clean authorization/fulfillment/expiry trigger, later weakened by first-party capture/reauthorization features and payment orchestration.
Strong minimum-spend shortfall economics, later weakened by cloud commitment managers and procurement/SaaS allocation tooling.
Excellent economics but current systems reconcile volume commitments, deficiency payments and make-up rights.
Promising pattern: two legitimate future uses already exist and a contractual or quota state changes which is economically optimal; detect before the decision and redirect existing activity.
Prepaid messaging credits plus scheduled sends created a good trigger; later search found mature multi-provider SMS routing/cost optimization layers.
GitHub/Taskman selected as permanent anchor for search state, evidence, rejected paths, scores, task results and conversation-derived knowledge.
Every recurring research run must read Taskman first and persist the full normalized result back to Taskman before completion.

Included/prepaid SaaS or API capacity approaches reset while already-planned deferrable workloads exist; clean trigger and measurable overage avoidance, but no single high-value non-AI/non-enrichment vertical with proven leakage was identified.

Provider-native app-store grace windows create a real net-margin choice for high-variable-cost apps, but this run showed the decision is app-wide/infrequent, relatively spreadsheetable and difficult to attribute for performance pricing.

Convert vendor refund promises/credit memos into expected receivables, match them to corporate card/bank credits, and escalate missing or short settlements before dispute deadlines. Strong per-event attribution and non-invasive intervention; leakage magnitude and incumbent overlap remain uncertain.
Exact tools already identify unused labels and automate carrier refunds/voids, including performance-priced recovery.

conversation_history.candidate: Prior-authorization expiry before scheduled service watchdog
conversation_history.summary: Current authorization tools already track expiry and explicitly flag authorizations that will expire before scheduled procedures.

current_leader.name: Corporate promised-refund settlement watchdog
current_leader.state_transition: vendor or merchant promises a refund or credit -> expected receivable is created from email/ERP/card context -> card or bank credit does not arrive, arrives short, or arrives late -> system detects mismatch before escalation/dispute deadline -> evidence-based recovery action -> recovered amount is measured
current_leader.why_survived: The event exists naturally in email, ERP, card and bank data; the intervention can remain read-only until escalation; the dollar delta is exact; performance pricing maps to each recovered receivable; consumer and single-merchant products validate the event, while broad enterprise reconciliation products create adjacent rather than yet-proven exact competition.
strongest_evidence: Consumer refund-matching tools prove that refund promises can be matched against bank activity and escalated when missing.
Single-merchant recovery tools prove bank matching plus dispute-draft generation can recover missing refunds.
Enterprise reconciliation software explicitly identifies missing or mismatched refunds, proving that the data can be reconciled at scale but also creating incumbent pressure.
Corporate card dispute processes commonly use finite windows and supporting-document requirements, creating an external intervention deadline.
current_leader.closest_threat: Broad reconciliation and spend-management platforms can already identify refund mismatches and could absorb promise-to-settlement tracking. The enterprise dollar pool of vendor-promised refunds that never or incorrectly settle is not yet quantified.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read authorized email/ERP/accounting/card/bank feeds; extract each refund promise as an expected receivable with amount/date/reference; match incoming credits including partial credits; flag overdue/short settlement; generate evidence and escalation/dispute draft. Do not move funds or sit on the payment path.
current_leader.monetization: Small percentage of objectively recovered missing/short refunds or fixed fee per recovered refund.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Need evidence that missing or short corporate refunds are frequent and large enough outside platform-specific reconciliation, and that broad reconciliation/expense suites do not already neutralize this narrow workflow.
current_leader.next_research_test: Quantify enterprise vendor-refund leakage and search exact B2B expected-refund-receivable software that ingests refund promises/credit memos, matches them to corporate card/bank credits, tracks deadlines, and recovers missing/short refunds on a performance basis. Kill if incumbents already do it end-to-end or leakage is trivial.

runner_ups.reason: Strong trigger and attribution but no proven high-value vertical yet.
Real economic tradeoff but infrequent/app-wide and hard to performance-price.
Real expiry but routing incumbents can absorb expiry awareness.

new_search_rules: A non-trivial configuration choice is still a weak tollbooth if it changes only occasionally; favor repeated unit-level events with per-event attribution.

Cross-system promised-value versus actual-settlement events are attractive because an unstructured promise can be converted into a machine-readable receivable and matched to objective cash/card settlement.
Finite dispute or claim deadlines strengthen intervention value only when the expected-value event is independently machine-readable.
